summary: I has the affected person as subject, whereas III has a persuader and a persuadee. III can take ḥḏoḏe as an ordinary reciprocal object without Detransitive morphology (PrS 20/12; PrS 21/2).
I agreement may have aʕm- for the counterpart or b- for persuasive words. The amount-sufficiency construction at 52/198 is assigned sense 2 independently of the uncertain segmentation pani.

III persuasion takes zero-marked, l-marked or suffixed human objects; d-marked content clauses and bare following content occur. 107/107 explicitly combines beneficiary -lux and object -yo, broadening the documented argument frame without a new sense.

III Infectum-wa in JTM 3.2/33 describes a habitual paid persuasion procedure; gifts or bribery are means, not a separate lexical sense. The Imperativ at 53/103 and Detransitive Infectum at PrS 77/61 supply missing boxes.

III Preterit maqnaʕle u taʕlo is morphologically active even though the German makes the fox the subject of ließ sich überreden. The supplied verse alone does not fully identify the omitted persuader; retain the quotation and raise the role assignment, rather than changing its box from the translation.
No idiom or light-verb construction requires a new collocation entry. Money and gifts are ordinary inducements; reciprocal persuasion is an object construction.
All 16 occurrences receive ordered decisions. Existing round-1 senses and boxes, including Imperativ and Infectum-wa, are not proposed again.

III Part act. maqnəʕono describes persuasive disposition rather than a completed persuasion event. It is provisionally filed in the available glossary box without claiming that a single adjectival token proves a productive paradigm.
I qunaʕwo has the satisfied person as subject and b əno as stimulus. III has persuader plus persuadee; institutions as objects are participant extensions, not new senses.

maqneʕunne and maqnəʕ commands differ in number/object expression; ordinary use of bribes or passports does not lexicalize a new meaning. maqnəʕile merits one unusual suffix example despite the already full ordinary Preterit cell.
The bənne at Jan 1.39/1717 may code persuadees or a broader engagement/means relation; it is recorded for review rather than asserted as a new lexical government.
The fox example in the inherited III Preterit remains a round-1 role question; Jan active patient examples do not supply the missing old-context evidence needed for an entry correction.
English quotations are supplied project machine translations. The word satisfaction is checked against qanaʕa and the b-stimulus context in Turoyo.

At 52/198, confirm pani as b-hani and reduced qənʕat as Infectum rather than a reduced Preterit Intransitive. The sufficiency reading is secure in context, but no definitive b- government is added for sense 2.
Confirm -lle with female patient in JTM 5.2/38, -alle in 24/121, and the two suffixes in 107/107.
In PrS 80/88 (= inherited prs 234/29), is the fox the zero-marked patient of an omitted persuader, or is another construction intended? Do not infer grammatical voice from the German alone.
Confirm alternate PrS reference numbering before any citation replacement there; unlike 60/222, it is not demonstrated to be a wrong quotation.
Is maqnəʕono (Jan 1.48/2142) a productive Part act. or a lexical agent adjective? Retain the attested spelling and provisional box.
Confirm the vowels of qunaʕwo and whether b əno is the normal stimulus coding for satisfaction; this independently supports round-1 I.2.
At Jan 1.39/1717 does bənne mark persuadees, the matter argued about, or the people through whom persuasion proceeds?
Resolve Maqnəʕənne at Jan 2.9/2080 and maqnəʕilən at Jan 1.46/2044 between contracted Preterit and Infectum/person analyses before adding paradigmatic examples.
Confirm pre-agent patient -i- in maqnəʕile at Jan 3.15/189; the active meaning is clearer than its segmentation.
Correct ihres to ihre before beiden Söhne.
rationale: Söhne is the plural subject of kamen and requires nominative ihre. The extra s is a grammatical typo also present in the supplied edition.

summary: Capitalize Hause in nach Hause.
rationale: Hause is a noun here; the supplied edition correctly has nach Hause.

summary: Jan independently supports the round-1 satisfaction sense: an officer is satisfied with the speaker, overtly b əno. This broadens the stimulus from possessed wealth to a person.
The persuadee can be the state, a political electorate or recruited informants. Money remains an ordinary b-marked inducement, already documented in round 1.
